posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
It seems profoundly weird to plaster "VisuStella products are banned from this jam!" over the rules.
If you have some kind of personal problem with that team, bringing it out publicly in a game jam like this seems unprofessional and begging to get your project mired down in drama instead of attracting people to submit games.
It also seems to be penalizing owners of MZ, who aren't being allowed to use the most ubiquitous plugins for that engine, while anyone using older software has free reign.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Just to offer the opinion, your rules read like you have not gone through any past, successful game jams to see how their rules were structured. You should not be trying to rewrite and revise things based on people's opinions.
And if you're running this by yourself (which is very unusual, most jams are run by a team so you have multiple judges for unbiased scoring, etc.), you should set the rules and not change them.
Changing things around while people are considering their participation and what they would make will likely result in them getting frustrated and deciding against it.

Why? Write one story quest, go from a town through a bit of world map through a dungeon that has a couple of levels, have some more story concluding it; with encounters, that should absolutely take an hour.

posts.author: MorteEternal
posts.body:
The Jam is now over.
Congratulations to the four entries that made it on time, and a big thank you to everyone who gave it their best effort. Your dedication and creativity have truly shone through, making this Jam a memorable event. It’s inspiring to see such passion and hard work from all participants. This has also been a learning experience for creating much better Jams in the future.
Looking ahead, I’m excited to announce that I will be hosting another Jam in the future. This upcoming event will feature a longer creation period and more flexible rules, allowing for greater creativity and participation. Additionally, we will be opening the doors to more RPG Maker versions, ensuring that everyone has the opportunity to showcase their talents. Stay tuned for more details about that Jam, and thank you once again for your incredible contributions!
GrayBardGaming and I are excited to dive into the submissions and begin our thorough review process. Stay tuned for updates!

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
I don't think that's it. Beregon gives a lot more time and doesn't have as strict a minimum playtime limit, and I think that was the bigger factor.
Asking people to make 30+ minutes in a week is a pretty hard ask. It is commonly said you need 100 hours to make the first hour of your game any good. So to get a good entry you would need a way to dedicate 50ish hours to this jam alone in one week. That's almost impossible while working full time as well.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: Didnt ATT_Turan say you could make an hour long game in two days of hobby time? Which is it?

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body: I said *GOOD* game. I could make a bad game in a day that is an hour long easily with the random dungeon generator.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
bgillisp said:
It is commonly said you need 100 hours to make the first hour of your game any good.
Click to expand...
I'm not familiar with the source of that quote, but I'm quite sure that's intended to be speaking of developing a professional-quality commercial game of decent length (although I'd
still
question the number pulled out of someone's butt, since the first hour of your game usually has the least mechanics in it).
And I'm sure whoever said it is including the hours spent on creating audio and graphical resources for that hour of gameplay, etc.
That's very different from whipping together an intentionally short product with already-provided limited resources.
That seems to be like claiming "It takes hundreds of hours to create a masterwork painting, so it's impossible for someone to choose to paint something of less intricacy faster."

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
In my experience though, no game whipped out in one week with say 30 min - 1 hour playtime is good. At all. Maybe someone will prove me wrong someday.
But in general I think the minimum play time and short time limit was the reason most did not enter.  Even the IGMC asked for about 1 hour playtime and it gave everyone a month on average. No idea why they thought they were going to do better than the IGMC.
